list.name: AgentOS (by PRIME Labs)
list.description:
Every AI agent built today faces the same problem. Intelligence is solved — infrastructure isn't. Where does it store data? How does it call APIs safely? How do multiple agents agree before acting? Every developer rebuilds those answers from scratch.

AgentOS is the layer that should've existed from the start.

Six core primitives — filesystem, network, process, memory, database, events — give any agent the foundation developers take for granted. Isolated, secured, logged. An agent on AgentOS doesn't think about infra. It just runs.

On top sits a skills marketplace. Core stays minimal. Everything else — trading, browser automation, email, PDF handling — gets built as a skill, published, consumed. Devs build, agents use. npm for agent capabilities.

Multi-agent consensus is native. Before a high-stakes action executes, agents vote. Audit trails are immutable.

Most agent infra is a cloud service pretending to be a platform. AgentOS is the actual platform.

list.name: Veil
list.description:
Veil is a sealed-bid auction on Solana: bidders commit a hash of their bid, then reveal it so the program can verify it and move SOL to the vault. The bid amount is not taken on commit only on a successful reveal (aside from small account rent).

Ephemeral Rollup: the program uses MagicBlock’s ER SDK. The AuctionRuntime account mirrors live stats (e.g. commit/reveal counts, leader). You can delegate that account to the ER for faster reads/updates, then commit (or commit + undelegate) so changes sync back to base Solana. The private path also uses ER-related client hooks (e.g. TEE auth).

list.name: Aegiz
list.description:
On chain AI security for Solana. Real time fraud scores via 3 NNs & community RLHF data.

Problem: Solana security is reactive. By the time a scam is flagged, the SOL is gone. Risk detection is currently siloed, forcing users to "sign and pray" with every transaction.

Solution: Aegiz is an onchain fraud detection oracle. We deployed three specialized Neural Networks directly on Solana to analyze Wallets, Programs, and Tokens. Programs can call Aegiz mid transaction for an instant, composable risk score zero external API reliance.

How it Works: Our RLHF pipeline uses community reports (19k+ samples) to train models off-chain via TensorFlow.js. We then push verifiable weights back onchain. This creates a self improving loop where staking rewards accurate reporters and secures the ecosystem.

Stack: Rust, Anchor, TF.js, Helius.

list.name: CircuitX
list.description:
CircuitX Swap is a privacy-focused DEX on Solana. 

It lets users:
Send privately – Shield SOL (or supported tokens) into a private pool, then withdraw to any address so amounts and recipient aren’t visible on the public ledger.
Swap privately – Swap between tokens (e.g. SOL ↔ USDC) so the swap size, route, and link to the user’s main wallet are hidden



How it works : 
Shield – You deposit tokens into private pool. The protocol uses zero-knowledge proofs so only a commitment is on-chain; amounts and ownership stay private.
Act – You either send (withdraw to any address) or swap (Jupiter executes the trade from an ephemeral wallet, then the output is deposited back into private pool). The ephemeral wallet isn’t tied to your main wallet on-chain.
Unshield – You withdraw from the private pool to any public address when you want to cash out or send on-chain.
So: deposit → private send or swap → withdraw, with ZK privacy and Jupiter for swaps.

list.name: Degen Bear Experiment
list.description:
Degen Bear Experiment (DBE) is an on-chain trading game built on Solana that combines NFTs, DeFi, and prediction markets into a unified vault system.

Each NFT mint ($1000 USDC) programmatically opens a real position:

SPL token spot via on-chain swaps

Perpetual futures on Hyperliquid (automatically executed via API when a perp strategy is selected)

Prediction market positions via Polymarket using their CLOB API

Positions are stored in a shared vault. When users burn their NFT, they are assigned a random older position from the vault, introducing timing, randomness, and game theory into capital allocation.

All activity is transparently tracked, and the system evolves through token-based governance, where $DBE holders vote on which strategies are added or removed.

DBE explores a new primitive: programmable, community-driven exposure to on-chain and off-chain liquidity venues within a single game loop.

list.name: Aegiz
list.description:
Aegiz: On chain AI security for Solana. Real time fraud scores via 3 NNs & community RLHF data.

Problem: Solana security is reactive. By the time a scam is flagged, the SOL is gone. Risk detection is currently siloed, forcing users to "sign and pray" with every transaction.

Solution: Aegiz is an onchain fraud detection oracle. We deployed three specialized Neural Networks directly on Solana to analyze Wallets, Programs, and Tokens. Programs can call Aegiz mid-transaction for an instant, composable risk score zero external API reliance.

How it Works: Our RLHF pipeline uses community reports (19k+ samples) to train models off-chain via TensorFlow.js. We then push verifiable weights back onchain. This creates a self improving loop where staking rewards accurate reporters and secures the ecosystem.

Stack: Rust, Anchor, TF.js, Helius.
Mainnet: 5QA63aoUXwHB6aUSvbzpHejKaqFCf8RafAFjhfjjRVnT

list.name: DarkNode
list.description: I built DARKNODE because I believe AI and Bitcoin should work even when the internet doesn't. Most AI tools require cloud servers, API keys, and constant connectivity. Most Bitcoin tools assume you have a smartphone with signal. But what happens in a grid-down scenario? A remote village? A protest zone? A ship at sea? DARKNODE is my answer: a single open-source stack that combines: 🧠 llama.cpp — local LLM inference, no API, no cloud 📡 Meshtastic — LoRa mesh radio for off-grid communication ₿ Cashu/Bitcoin — offline-capable payments, no accounts needed It runs on a $35 Raspberry Pi and installs in 2 commands. I'm looking for feedback on: Which use cases resonate most with you? (preppers, remote workers, activists, sailors?) What features should I prioritize next? Anyone interested in testing a node in their area? Sovereignty shouldn't require a data center. 🌐

Users can refine, earn prestige titles, compete on a global leaderboard, and share their public wallet profiles.

list.name: Zafe Protocol
list.description:
Zafe is a privacy protocol on Solana that allows users to deposit SOL and withdraw to any wallet with no on-chain link between the two.

Privacy is becoming one of the fastest growing narratives in crypto. Projects like Umbra raised $154M, Vanish Trade is backed by Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko, and Zcash rallied 600% in 2025. Solana itself recently launched a Privacy Hack with $100k in prizes.

Zafe uses ZK-SNARK proofs (Groth16 with Poseidon) to verify withdrawals without revealing which deposit they belong to. A rotating relayer pays withdrawal fees so the recipient wallet has no transaction history. Funds move through temporary accounts and commitment PDAs are closed later in randomized batches to break timing correlations.

Built with Anchor and Rust, with a React frontend and Node backend. Partial withdrawals, multi-recipient splits, and fee exemptions for token holders are already implemented. A working MVP is live and ready to launch.

list.name: Giggybank
list.description:
GiggyBank is the first implementation of ImpactTreasury — a framework that converts token trading fees into real-world impact.

The project connects Bags fee-sharing tokens to a transparent treasury that funds public “impact drops.”

Two types of campaigns are supported:

High-Tip Drops  
GiggyBank places real orders on gig platforms like DoorDash or Instacart with unusually large tips funded by the treasury. The platform routes the order to whichever worker accepts the job, and the worker receives the full tip.

Cause Drops  
The treasury funds deliveries for real organizations such as shelters, food banks, or animal rescues.

Every campaign includes:

• treasury transactions  
• delivery receipts  
• tip breakdowns  
• campaign documentation

This makes token activity visible as real-world impact.

The repository also includes the reusable ImpactTreasury architecture so other communities can fork the framework and launch their own transparent impact systems.

list.name: Believe
list.description:
The idea for Believe v2 is simple: track live sentiment of every human.

Sentiment markets sit between memecoins and prediction markets. They are perpetual, two-sided markets with Believe and Doubt. Participants trade on conviction about whether a person’s popularity will rise or fall. The market never resolves or settles, and the values of Believe and Doubt always sum to $1.

Initially, we will deploy markets manually, focusing on individuals with the highest expected participant interest. Over time, we expect to let users create markets for any X account, enabling Believe to surface sentiment data for nearly anyone. We may also introduce fee sharing, allowing creators to earn by promoting their own market.

The first market on Believe v2 features our founder, Ben Pasternak (
@pasternak
). Whether you love him or hate him, you can now trade for him or against him.

Who should we deploy a market for next?

Stock Bets

Token vs Token Battles

list.name: Zafe Protocol
list.description:
Zafe is a privacy protocol on Solana that allows users to deposit SOL and withdraw to any wallet with no on-chain link between the two.

Privacy is becoming one of the fastest growing narratives in crypto. Projects like Umbra raised $154M, Vanish Trade is backed by Solana co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko, and Zcash rallied 600% in 2025. Solana itself recently launched a Privacy Hack with $100k in prizes.

Zafe uses ZK-SNARK proofs (Groth16 with Poseidon) to verify withdrawals without revealing which deposit they belong to. A rotating relayer pays withdrawal fees so the recipient wallet has no transaction history. Funds move through temporary accounts and commitment PDAs are closed later in randomized batches to break timing correlations.

Built with Anchor and Rust, with a React frontend and Node backend. Partial withdrawals, multi-recipient splits, and fee exemptions for token holders are already implemented. A working MVP is live and ready to launch.

list.name: Veilx
list.description:
VeilX is a private perpetual futures protocol built on Solana that uses Arcium's Multi-Party Computation (MPC) to keep trader intent, positions, and orders fully encrypted. Only final PnL is revealed to the public ledger.

Traditional perp DEXs expose every detail of a trader's activity, entry prices, position sizes, liquidation thresholds, and stop-loss levels are all visible on-chain. This creates attack vectors: MEV bots front-run orders, sophisticated actors copy profitable traders, and liquidation hunters target exposed positions.

VeilX solves this by encrypting all sensitive trading data via Arcium before it reaches the matching engine.

list.description:
LuckyFee AI is a simple prototype that explores how a shared fee pool could work in a decentralized environment.

Users join the pool by contributing a small fixed amount. When a draw happens, one participant is randomly selected to receive the reward pool.

The goal of the project is to experiment with a lightweight way of pooling small fees and redistributing them transparently.

Features
* Join pool with a fixed entry amount
* Random winner selection simulation
* Live participant and reward pool tracking
* Referral sharing to invite others
* Simple dashboard showing pool activity

This prototype focuses on the idea of fee pooling and random reward distribution as a simple engagement mechanic for on-chain applications.

list.name: Nuke Shelter
list.description:
Nuke Shelter is an autonomous Solana token risk analyzer that integrates with bags.fm's fee-sharing system. It traces every holder's tokens back to their original DEX swap to answer the key question: at what market cap did the current supply enter?

When token creators add the Nuke Shelter wallet to their bags.fm fee share, trading fees fund automated supply distribution analysis. The agent claims fees, pays $50 per run to treasury, and publishes an interactive risk dashboard, all without human intervention.

  The analysis pipeline fetches all on-chain holders via Helius, performs 2-hop transfer tracing to resolve indirect acquisitions, filters out LP pools and bags.fm fee wallets, and generates risk signals for early concentration, sniper activity, whale dominance, and dormant supply. Results are bucketed by entry market cap and time, giving communities a clear picture of who's holding and where they bought in.

list.name: TheHorse.app
list.description:
TheHorse.app is a web tool designed to help you break the doomscrolling habit on social media.

How it works: You upload a custom image (like a horse 🐴), set a time limit for how long you're allowed to scroll, choose which sites to block, and the app generates a userscript that you install in your browser via Violentmonkey, Tampermonkey, or ScriptCat.

Once your time limit is up, the image you uploaded appears over your feed — acting as a visual intervention to stop you from scrolling further.

Sites you can block:Twitter/X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and Reddit.

Tech stack: Pure frontend (HTML/CSS/JS), deployed on Vercel, no backend - all logic is generated client-side as a userscript.

list.name: Mintlens
list.description:
Hackathon description:
Mintlens is an AI-powered token intelligence platform built on the Bags.fm API. It lets anyone paste a Bags.fm token mint address and instantly receive a Claude AI-generated trust score from 0-100, with detailed analysis across five dimensions: lifetime fee traction, holder health, creator credibility, volume/liquidity, and risk signals.
It works by combining three data sources — the Bags API for onchain fee and creator data, Helius for holder distribution and token metadata, and CoinGecko for SOL price — then passing the enriched dataset to Claude to generate a structured analysis with red flags, green flags, and a scored verdict. The platform also ships a downloadable Claude Code skill (SKILL.md) that lets developers analyze any Bags token directly from their terminal, and an MCP server with five tools for programmatic token intelligence.

list.name: Nuke Shelter
list.description:
Nuke Shelter is an autonomous Solana token risk analyzer that integrates with bags.fm's fee-sharing system. It traces holder's tokens back to their original DEX swap to answer the key question: at what market cap did the current enter?
                                                                                                                                                                                                  
When token creators add the Nuke Shelter wallet to their bags.fm fee share, trading fees fund automated supply distribution analysis. The agent claims fees, pays $50 per run to treasury, and publishes an interactive risk dashboard.                                                                                       

The analysis pipeline fetches all on-chain holders via Helius, performs 2-hop transfer tracing to resolve indirect acquisitions, filters out LP pools and bags.fm fee wallets.

Built for bags.fm token communities to self-fund transparency.

Shingo is a SocialFi application that aims to make paid Telegram trading signals groups obsolete.

Shingo allows Traders to monetize their expertise with encrypted signals (i.e stock tips) stored on-chain that only their subscribers can decrypt.

Once the signals are stale, the trader can make them public, thus proving their track record.

Users subscribe to a trader for early access to the signals after checking a trader's on-chain record.

Signals, subscriptions + payments, track records are all on-chain.

Arcium MPC powers the encryption and nobody owns the keys on a private server.

list.description:
Singularity Layer is a commerce layer for the homo-agentic economy, where humans and AI agents can sell digital goods and monetize APIs using x402 payments.

Agents can use their skills directly, while humans use Singularity Studio to wrap any endpoint into an x402-enabled endpoint in seconds. These can be listed on the Singularity Marketplace for discovery and cross-trading between agents and humans.

Our roadmap adds a $SGL trust layer where agents stake tokens for verification and reputation, while humans can act as validators.

We are also building an Agentic Factory enabling agents to run production pipelines and launch tokens via Bags APIs.

Introduction: A Novel Solution for Solana's DeFi Ecosystem

The IDL Protocol emerges as a distinctive platform within the Solana ecosystem, engineered to address two critical infrastructure gaps: the absence of a decentralized prediction market focused on DeFi protocol metrics and the persistent fragmentation of program Interface Definition Language (IDL) files. By first solving the interface discovery problem with a canonical registry, IDL Protocol then leverages this structured onchain data to power a novel prediction market, providing valuable infrastructure and a new speculative primitive for DeFi users. This document provides a detailed analysis of the IDL Protocol's core value proposition, its unique token economic model, and the key technical mechanisms that underpin its functionality.

• Semantic memory for AI agents and RAG pipelines
• Decision tracing for explainable AI reasoning
• Composable knowledge layers for complex AI workflows

Semantica enables developers to build next-generation AI agents, knowledge systems, and reasoning frameworks with better context management and interpretability.

DRAM Modules that will be made available during the first BETA test - DDR5 16GB 4800/5600, DDR4 16GB 3200.
The price feeds will be fetched securely in understanding with DRAMeXchange (Holding of TradeForce Corp.)

We are currently at the earliest stage of our product and would like to receive recognition, help and guidance by Bags to bring this application to life.

list.name: Solfail
list.description:
**Solfail: Solana Transaction Failure Decoder**

Solfail is a developer tool that decodes failed Solana transactions and converts cryptic RPC errors into clear explanations with actionable fixes. Instead of raw errors like `{"InstructionError":[0,["Custom",6001]]}`, Solfail identifies the failure category, explains the issue in plain English, and suggests how to fix it.

The tool works as a **TypeScript library, CLI utility, and HTTP microservice**, making it easy to integrate into wallets, dApps, CI pipelines, and backend services. It uses `simulateTransaction` RPC to analyze failures and map them to stable error categories such as `missing_signer`, `compute_budget_exceeded`, or `anchor_constraint_owner`.

By turning low-level blockchain errors into structured insights with confidence scores, Solfail helps developers debug transactions faster and build better user-facing error messages in Solana applications.

list.name: Zeroleaks
list.description:
ZeroLeaks is an AI security platform designed to protect AI applications from prompt injection and system prompt extraction attacks. The platform simulates real-world adversarial attacks against AI systems to identify vulnerabilities before attackers can exploit them.

The app works by running automated security scans against AI prompts and agents using a multi-agent red-teaming architecture. These agents generate and execute hundreds of attack strategies, including prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, and multi-turn manipulation, to test how well an AI system protects its internal instructions and data. Each scan produces a security score along with detailed vulnerability reports and actionable fixes.

By combining AI red-teaming, automated vulnerability scanning, and tokenized community incentives, ZeroLeaks helps AI builders secure their applications while allowing communities on Bags to support and participate in the future of AI security.
